name: Poseidon
summary: God of the sea, earthquakes, and horses. Brother of Zeus and Hades, ruler of the waters after the three divided the cosmos following the Titanomachy.
cultural_context: Poseidon was especially important to coastal communities, sailors, and horse-breeding regions. His worship recognized the sea as a source of wealth and danger, while his title 'Earth-Shaker' acknowledged the destructive force of earthquakes.
origin_story: Like his siblings, Poseidon was swallowed at birth by his father Cronus and later freed when Zeus forced Cronus to disgorge his children. After the Olympians' victory over the Titans, the three brothers, Zeus, Poseidon, and Hades, drew lots for dominion over the cosmos. Poseidon received the sea.
achievements: Ruled and controlled the seas, able to calm or violently stir storms
Contested with Athena for patronage of Athens, striking the Acropolis to produce a saltwater spring, but lost to her gift of the olive tree
Fathered numerous offspring, including the Cyclops Polyphemus
Caused the storms and delays that plagued Odysseus's journey home after his son Polyphemus was blinded
Created or fathered horses in several traditions, linking the sea god with speed, power, and royal status
Supported the Greeks or Trojans in different myths while remaining a dangerous and unpredictable divine force

signature_quote.text: I am Poseidon, shaker of the earth and lord of the sea.
signature_quote.note: The titles express Poseidon's dangerous dual power over the sea, storms, horses, and earthquakes.
